newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INTERVIEW-Summit Valhalla tests acceptable.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Summit Valhalla tests acceptable.

text.p: Summit Gold NL said on Tuesday that uranium oxide recoveries from its Valhalla prospect in northern Queensland had shown that acceptable recoveries could be achieved.
Summit said in a statement that Metcon Laboratories had reported uranium oxide recoveries from alkaline and acid leach tests of 59 to 63 percent for the Valhalla mineralisation.
"We've still got a bit of work to do there, but it looks to me as if the nature of the ore is not refractory," Summit chairman Colin Beyer told Reuters in a telephone interview.

"In other words, if the uranium is locked in refractory rock, it's very difficult to get it out. We were concerned that it might be a refractory type ore and it turns out not to be, so that's really half the battle," Beyer added.
Summit said it looked as if acceptable recoveries from Valhalla could be achieved, but Beyer said other techniques would be tried to increase the recovery rate to over 80 percent.
"It's probably commercial at lower rates, in fact many of the uranium facilities around the world recover at a lower rate, but what we have to do is recover it at an economic cost."
To that end, Summit was trying to reduce the consumption of acid used in the leaching process.

Summit was hopeful that Valhalla would emerge as a commercial operation but that it aimed to continue enhancing recoveries until it received definitive answers. Summit's partner in the project is Perth-based Resolute.
Percussion drilling along a two kilometre gold arsenic soil anomaly at Carrick, in central Otago, New Zealand, started early this month and assay results are expected over the next week.
Geologically, Carrick is similar in structure to the successful Macraes Mining Co Ltd operation at nearby Macraes Flat.

Summit said its joint venture partner CRA Exploration Pty had reported anomalous base metal results from the Isa North drill programme, while Sons of Gwalia Ltd had reported encouraging gold intersections at Admiral Hill in West Australia.
Summit shares, which last year shot up to NZ$0.85 from a low of 7.3 cents, traded today at NZ$0.51, up two cents.
Summit is 33-34 percent owned by its directors since a management buyout in early 1996.
Perth-based managing director Alan Eggers holds about 10-12 percent of the company, which is a "junior" explorer listed in Australia as well as in New Zealand.
